images.title: Sides start at three
images.purpose: Show that regular polygons have 3, 4, 5, 6 sides and so on, counting numbers from 3.
images.composition: Four polygons in a 2 by 2 arrangement with wide spacing, each with a name label, and a note below.
images.exact_structure: Four regular polygons in a 2 by 2 arrangement, similar size and wide gaps: triangle (3 sides), square (4 sides), pentagon (5 sides), hexagon (6 sides). The triangle is amber #E69F00 to mark the start, the other three teal #0072B2. A name and side count label beside each shape. One note centred below. Exactly 4 shapes.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a polygon with the wrong number of sides
images.takeaway: The number of sides counts up from 3.
images.description: Four regular polygons with 3, 4, 5 and 6 sides labelled with their names, the triangle in amber as the start.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the sides of each polygon and say where the counting starts.

image_decisions.why: Four shapes are enough to show the counting numbers from 3 behind the names.
